rounds.text: The valuation of Antony Waste Handling Cell Ltd is disconnected from its underlying fundamental reality, trading at an extreme price-to-earnings ratio of 106x and a price-to-book multiple of 3.22x [E1, E2]. This expensive pricing is compounded by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value calculation pointing to Rs 43 per share against a market price of Rs 425, resulting in a staggering negative margin of safety of -889.3% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's market price demands an unrealistic 31.9% earnings growth, while the rules-based screen firmly scores the stock a 26 out of 100 with a sell recommendation [E45, E63]. Profitability metrics lag sector benchmarks considerably, highlighted by a depressed return on equity of 3.7% in the filed statements and a median return on equity of just 3% over the last three years [E9, E13, E26]. Balance sheet risks are acute as borrowings surged to Rs 263 Cr in March 2026 from only Rs 21 Cr a year earlier, contributing to flags for a low interest coverage ratio [E37, E60]. Institutional capital is actively fleeing the counter, evidenced by negative money flow and a reduction in both foreign and domestic institutional holdings [E40, E41, E42]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reaches 1721% alongside robust operating cash flows of Rs 66 Cr and a tailwind score of +0.93 in the utilities sector [E17, E33, E74].
